text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the median 20-session forward return was 2.96%, with a mean of 2.39% and a standard deviation of 6.9%. The distribution is slightly left-skewed, meaning the downside tail is thicker than the upside, and 32% of those analogs finished below zero. The single number to anchor on is that 2.96% median, which represents the central tendency of what happened next when this specific combination of features appeared historically.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 39 distinct sessions across 30 symbols because the current state is defined by a sharp compression in short-term volatility against a backdrop of elevated longer-term realised volatility and a massive crude oil move. Specifically, the 5d/20d volatility ratio is 0.489 (z-score -1.217), while the 20-session realised volatility sits at 48.97% (z-score 0.983). WTI crude changed 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124). Dollar volume is depressed, with a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score of -1.558 (used as -1.026). TSLA is trading 364.27, sitting -26.98% from its 52-week high and -14.35% off its 60-session peak. These features, weighted 30% for name-specific price/vol dynamics, 20% for market, 20% for macro, 10% for crypto, and 20% for event timing, map closest to episodes like TMO on 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4262) and SLB on 2026-08-04 (distance 0.4336). Only one retrieved analog is TSLA itself, from 2025-08-07.

[history]
Over the 20-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced returns ranging from -11.47% to 15.49%. The interquartile range spans from -1.25% at the 25th percentile to 6.87% at the 75th percentile, with the 10th percentile at -8.68% and the 90th at 10.51%. The skew is -0.288. In 68% of the episodes, the forward return was above zero; in 32%, it was below. The bad tail is dominated by China ADR names: LI on 2025-09-22 returned -11.47% with a max adverse excursion of -13.16%, and PDD on 2025-07-08 dropped -3.98% intraday despite finishing up 5.94%. BABA on 2025-07-01 suffered a -9% drawdown before settling at 2.99%. On the upside, NKE on 2023-10-10 returned 12.03% without any adverse excursion, and SLB on 2026-08-04 returned 12.48%. Technology makes up 12 of the 50 analogs, and the year 2025 accounts for 20 of them, concentrating the sample heavily in recent history.

[tails]
A position can finish near the median and still be un-holdable through the path. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -3.53%. The 25th percentile of adverse excursions reached -7.38%, and the 10th percentile hit -10.99%. Conversely, the median maximum favourable excursion was 6.73%, reaching 9.45% at the 75th percentile and 14.07% at the 90th, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.91. Looking strictly at drawdown breaches during the 20 sessions: 40% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown, 14% breached a 10% drawdown, and 0% breached 15% or 20%.

[stress]
Fourteen stress scenarios were run; none were skipped. Against the baseline median of 2.96%, three rate-and-macro regimes materially worsen the picture. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario produced a median forward return of -7.83% (delta -10.79%), with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yielded a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%) and a 50% breach probability; caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash showed a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%) but a 72.9% probability of a 10% drawdown, with the 10th percentile reaching -30.58%; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime, not a forecast.

Event-driven shocks also degrade the baseline. The earnings release day scenario printed a median of -1.18% (delta -4.14%) with a 48% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The 2025-04 tariff shock produced a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%) and a 61.5% breach probability; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The carry unwind of 2024-08-05 had a benign terminal median of -0.03% (delta -2.99%) but a 44.4% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not.

The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue produced a median of 2.62% (delta -0.34%) with a 14% breach probability; caveat: blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution, and a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. The regional bank stress of 2023-03 actually improved the median to 3.07% (delta +0.11%); caveat: very short window, so the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2022 inflation/rate bear, because its median of -7.83% and delta of -10.79% directly stress the multiple-rich profile implied by TSLA's 48.97% realised volatility; the earnings release day, because with 45 calendar days to the next release (z-score 0.663), an earnings print will likely fall within the 20-session horizon, and its 48% breach probability across 50 analogs shows how binary that event is; and the 2025-04 tariff shock, because the 19.24% WTI move and the heavy weighting of China ADRs (7 of 50 analogs) in the retrieval set make trade-policy cross-contagion a live risk, evidenced by its 61.5% breach probability across 26 analogs. A reader should distrust the concentration of the year 2025, which supplies 20 of the 50 analogs, compressing the historical variance into a narrow recent window. No scenario contradicts the positive direction of the baseline median; all either worsen it or leave it roughly intact.

[limits]
This analysis is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source. The honest verdict from the engine's validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test." The conformal interval achieves 87.4% out-of-sample coverage against an 80% target, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name benchmark is -3.4%.

For path risk, the engine targets a 10% drawdown breach level. Out of sample, the realised breach rate was 16.2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 17.2%, leaving a calibration gap of 1.03 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 2.85. The Brier score of the analog share was 0.1335. Compared to the volatility reflection benchmark (0.136), the paired difference confidence interval spans zero (-0.0144 to 0.0102), so the comparison is unresolved. Compared to the same-name calibration (0.1333), the interval also spans zero (-0.0087 to 0.0097), remaining unresolved. Only against the pooled calibration (0.1378) does the analog score better, with 82% of queries favouring the analog, though the interval (-0.0128 to 0.0041) still technically spans zero.

The wrapper status is measured. On the primary venue (Bitget official MCP, TSLA/USDT RWA perpetual), the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, yet 44.55% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9637 and a tracking error of 98 bp/day. The basis band is -0.51% to 0.39%, and the spread is 0.26 bps. Caveat: a fair perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; at 98 bp/day of tracking error it carries its own idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis means your exit price differs from the reference close the analog distribution is built on.

For the return layer on that wrapper, across 6 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend return was -0.312%, the 10th percentile was -1.13%, and the standard deviation was 1.0081%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.6715%, and 0% of those weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
